title: Register a Fargate task definition and break its network mode
kills: "A Fargate task can use any network mode, as a task on an EC2 instance can."
cost: $0: there is no additional charge for Amazon ECS, and a registered task definition runs no task, so Fargate bills no vCPU or memory.
cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day: a task definition that runs no task has no charge. Delete it anyway, so that no unused task definition stays in the account.
read_only_alternative: In an account where you cannot create resources, read an existing task definition: aws ecs list-task-definitions lists the revisions, and aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition <TASK_DEFINITION> --query "taskDefinition.{Mode:networkMode,Requires:requiresCompatibilities}" shows its network mode. A task definition that requires FARGATE shows awsvpc. The commands change nothing.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Register a task definition for Fargate with the bridge network mode, the smallest task size and one public web server container.
steps.command: aws ecs register-task-definition --family saa-containers-t03 --requires-compatibilities FARGATE --network-mode bridge --cpu 256 --memory 512 --container-definitions '[{"name":"saa-web","image":"public.ecr.aws/docker/library/httpd:latest","essential":true}]' --tags key=book,value=saa key=task,value=containers-t03
steps.expect: An error (a client exception) that names the network mode. No task definition is registered.
steps.predict: On an EC2 instance, a task can use the bridge network mode. Does ECS accept bridge mode in a task definition that requires FARGATE?
steps.explain: Amazon ECS tasks for AWS Fargate require the awsvpc network mode, which [provides each task with an elastic network interface](../facts/fargate.md#fargate-requires-awsvpc-network-mode). You asked for FARGATE in the required compatibilities, so ECS checked the task definition against Fargate and returned the error. Tasks that use Fargate do not support [all of the Amazon ECS task definition parameters](../facts/fargate.md#fargate-launch-type-requires-task-definition-config) that are available.

steps.text: Fix it: register the same task definition with the awsvpc network mode. The shell keeps the ARN of the new revision in TD_ARN.
steps.command: aws ecs register-task-definition --family saa-containers-t03 --requires-compatibilities FARGATE --network-mode awsvpc --cpu 256 --memory 512 --container-definitions '[{"name":"saa-web","image":"public.ecr.aws/docker/library/httpd:latest","essential":true}]' --tags key=book,value=saa key=task,value=containers-t03
steps.expect: No output: the shell keeps the task definition ARN in TD_ARN.

steps.text: Read the network mode, the required compatibilities, the task size and the status of the new revision.
steps.expect: Mode awsvpc, Requires FARGATE, Cpu 256, Memory 512 and Status ACTIVE.

cleanup.text: Deregister the revision. Its status becomes INACTIVE. If your CloudShell session ended, TD_ARN is empty: set it again to the ARN that aws ecs list-task-definitions --family-prefix saa-containers-t03 prints.
Delete the deregistered revision. ECS marks it DELETE_IN_PROGRESS until no task or service uses it, and here none does.

verify.expect: An empty list. If the task definition ARN still shows, ECS has not finished the deletion: wait one minute and run the command again. A second check without tags: aws ecs describe-task-definition --task-definition $TD_ARN returns an error after the deletion has finished.

still_costs: Nothing: a task definition that runs no task has no charge, and there is no additional charge for Amazon ECS. Delete it anyway, so that no unused task definition stays in the account.
